name: Praxis
description:
We are in a moment in history where entrepreneurs have disproportionate influence on everything from the social problems they work on to what they consume, practice, believe, and desire. As Jack Dorsey, founder of Twitter and Square, recently declared on the cover of Forbes, "The most efficient means to spread an idea today is corporate structure." Moreover, according to the Kauffman Foundation, 54% of millennials have started an organization or have the desire to start one. Given all of this, we believe the future of our world depends largely on the ventures the next generation creates.

To create an institution for this context, we've created Praxis as a venture group, structured as a non-profit, that focuses on equipping and resourcing a growing portfolio of faith-motivated entrepreneurs who have committed their lives to cultural and social impact, renewing the spirit of their age one organization at a time. Praxis was conceived in 2010 by Dave Blanchard, then a Principal Designer at IDEO, and Josh Kwan, the Director of International Giving for the David Weekley Family Foundation, and developed in collaboration with Q, a learning community that mobilizes Christians to advance the common good in society.

Each year, Praxis welcomes 12 businesses and 12 nonprofits into their two Accelerator programs, where they provide the top decision-makers in these organizations with the knowledge, network, and personal discipleship necessary to build sustainable, high-impact organizations. In the summer of 2014, they'll also launch Praxis Academy, a summer program focused on training Christ-following undergraduates at the intersection of faith, startups, and culture. Academy graduates will have a chance to apply for their Future Founders program, where they'll have a unique opportunity to do a summer apprenticeship with their Accelerator alumni.
locations: Union Square, New York, NY, USA

name: Corner to Corner
description:
Corner to Corner co-creates economic participation and growth with underestimated Nashvillians through knowledge, tools, and networks. We are based in Nashville, tackling economic inequity from its roots: through early opportunities for young creators and by working with early-stage entrepreneurs.

We transform the joy of creation into economic flourishing. Starting in middle school, we increase knowledge-based learning through Script to Screen. We engage entrepreneurs at the earliest stage with Academy participants.

Script to Screen is a creative after-school program that helps kids fall in love with reading through their love of movies. Our young creators watch a popular film while reading the script at the same time and collaborate with their peers to create an entire movie – from plot points to dialogue and everything in between. Literacy is a key factor in predicting future earnings, with a solid proficient reader earning $29,000 on average more than peers not reading at a proficient level. In collaboration with Vanderbilt, pilot data found that our program boosted students’ confidence with reading, and 55% of our young creators grew a full grade level.

The Academy is a 10-week program that equips community members with the skills they need to plan, start, and grow their own small businesses. The Academy helps neighbors create a sustainable economic engine for their families and community. The Academy has graduated nearly 700 entrepreneurs, each in various stages of small business ownership, and 88% of our Academy Alumni are Black women. In 2021 alone, our entrepreneurs were responsible for putting $13 million back into the neighborhood economy here in Nashville.

The Academy Amplified is our supplemental program dedicated to offering our Academy Alumni continued support through opportunities like Business to Business mentoring, video marketing classes, and our new pilot small loan program, The Academy Invested, among others.

We form entrepreneurially minded young adults into transformative leaders and culture creators who have the wisdom and experience they need to face the future’s most critical challenges. Our motto is Quaerare (to seek), Amare (to love), Aedificare (to create).

Offering a single, rigorous Bachelor's degree in Liberal Arts and Entrepreneurship, Hildegard College is action-oriented and steeped in the Christian tradition. We replace lectures, tests, and quizzes with Socratic small-group discussions, real-world projects, work experience with Civic Partners, and 1-on-1 faculty mentors. Our $16,000/year tuition, donor-funded scholarships, Homestay program, and work-study options make this high-quality college experience both accessible and affordable.

Applications are open for the 24-25 academic year. Visit our website to book a campus visit, request more information, and apply.

Hildegard also offers learning opportunities for high school students and adult learners. Great Works Seminars offer learners of all ages the opportunity to exercise civil discourse as they study the ideas that have shaped history. description:
The Justice Defense Fund (JDF) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit committed to empowering survivors of tech-facilitated sex trafficking, child sexual abuse material (CSAM), and image-based sexual abuse to seek justice through strategic litigation and advocacy. As a non-partisan and non-religious organization, we champion broad support for governmental and corporate policies to prevent online sexual crime.

Through our two strategic programs, Public Pressure Campaigns and Litigation & Survivor Support, JDF is dedicated to ending impunity for abusers and bringing justice to victims of online sexual crime.

Public Pressure Campaigns: JDF brings significant public pressure and accountability to abusers, their enablers, and government officials, compelling them to take action. JDF educates legislators, corporations, and the public to advocate for the adoption of laws and policies that prevent the monetization and distribution of online sex trafficking, child sexual abuse material, and image-based sexual abuse.

Litigation & Survivor Support: JDF supports civil litigation where needed and helps survivors access the costly and historically unequal legal system by supporting their pursuit of justice holistically. Our team of licensed experts in survivor care provides access to support and advocacy services.

As we believe that every person, no matter the challenges he/she is facing, has the right to be productive, have a decent job, and earn a living, ProAbled was launched to boost a shift in society’s mindset from limiting capacities of people with physical disabilities to creating opportunities for them to prove that they are PRO-fessionally Able.

ProAbled has 2 departments working together to offer a holistic inclusive solution:

- ProAbled Academy: Provides HRs and managers in companies, architects, and engineers with different consulting and training certificates in inclusive recruitment and inclusive design. In addition, ProAbled Academy provides a work readiness program for persons with disabilities or financial challenges aiming to get employed. 
- ProAbled Recruit: An online recruitment platform specialized in supporting companies to find the right candidates for their job vacancies among ProAbled candidates with disabilities.

ProAbled has supported 1,000 beneficiaries among companies, persons with disabilities, NGOs, INGOs, academic, and public institutions. It is currently scaling internationally by building new partnerships and providing its services in several countries.
